answer: In PoA, each identity is verified by a Wesolowski VDF whose output depends on a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings. Because every square requires the preceding result, an attacker simulating multiple clones cannot parallelize each chain across GPUs to reduce its elapsed time; every clone incurs its own sequential delay. This strict physical time bottleneck makes Sybil identities costly, whether labeled umber, sable, or juniper.
